results.title: Busabase: The general system of record for AI agents | Product Hunt
results.content:
Connect agents like Claude Code, Grok Bot, Muse, OpenClaw, Manus, Hermes, Buda or Codex via MCP, OpenAPI, or CLI. You decide what each agent can read or change, and which updates need review. You can also see what changed and who changed it.  
  
With your agents and tools connected, you can automate workflows like:  
  
• Software development — agents turn support feedback into tasks, write and test the code, deploy updates, and use new feedback to start the next cycle.  
• SEO — agents monitor traffic and search trends, use the results to improve the content plan, write the next article in a shared CMS, and repeat. [...] I'd start with one small task. Pick a type of record, give the agent the access it needs, and decide whether its updates can go through directly or need review. Then check the result in the UI.

Your team chooses what becomes shared. Connecting an agent doesn't automatically import everyone's private chats or local files.

What business record would you let an agent update first? Which changes would you still want to review yourself?

how does it handle conflicts? like if claude code and codex both touch the same record within a few minutes, does the second one just overwrite or does it go to review

Report

Seeyou Chan

Busabase

@mi\_leeli Thankyou, Mi.   
  
If both agents start from the same version and change the same field to different values, the merge is blocked and the conflict is flagged for review and resolution. You can also set permissions to require review for all agent changes.

The workflow is a bit like Git, but tailored to business data such as customer records and project updates.

What kind of business data are you planning to maintain? Knowing your use case would help me suggest how Busabase could fit your workflow.

@mathew\_james2 thanks for the comment, I often find myself wanting to massage my perfect change to commit. Still improving on it just by using it daily - for example yesterday I found a use case to allow users to open a review from “main” to “main” branch just to see these uncommitted changes. I wanted to push directly to main. In previous release of the app I was blocking reviews pointing to the same branch.

Report [...] I need, is my local GitHub I want that GitHub code review experience but before a commit is made, here on my computer. A single place where all my agents and I, can talk about code changes. So I build GitWarren. It’s a local, PR-like code review app that works directly with your working tree. I can review committed, staged, unstaged and untracked changes, leave inline comments, and organize the work into actual reviews without having to push anything anywhere. What I really like, is that I can just connect whatever AI I use at the moment through MCP and have a coherent experience without this mundane copy-pasting. results.title: AgentGrid: Your AI agents team, terminals, notes: one infinite canvas | Product Hunt
results.content:
What converted me was restart anxiety.   
  
Every system update meant losing all my Claude Code sessions. AgentGrid saves your entire workspace: every agent, every session, mapped visually on a 2D canvas. Restart, reopen, everything's exactly where you left it. I haven't lost a session since, and honestly we don't talk about that feature enough.

Once I was in, the rest clicked: an infinite canvas where your agents are panes you can watch. You spawn role-based workers (builder, QA, reviewer, devops…), and an orchestrator agent runs the loop: build → review → fix → validate, while you steer and take the final review.

Terminals, browsers, code, git and notes live on the same canvas, so "what is my AI doing?" is a glance, not an interrogation. [...] AgentGrid
